summary: a scientific task's tolerance by the person's standing rule: the reference's stated uncertainty, otherwise half a unit in the last digit it prints

inputs.name: printed
inputs.meaning: the reference value as its source prints it, as text, its last digit kept as printed (a trailing zero included); in the quantity's unit

inputs.name: stated_uncertainty
inputs.meaning: the uncertainty the source states for that value, in the quantity's unit, or null where it states none

outputs.name: tolerance
outputs.meaning: the tolerance, in the quantity's unit; null, with why, where neither input gives one

outputs.name: from
outputs.meaning: stated_uncertainty or last_printed_digit: which of the rule's two ways gave it; null where none did

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why no tolerance was given, or null

validity: one reference value of one quantity. The stated uncertainty, where there is one, is taken as handed: which uncertainty a source states (a standard error, the spread between its refinement levels) is the reader's to say. The last printed digit is read off the text as printed, so a trailing zero counts and a number already stored as a float has lost its printed form; an integer printed with trailing zeros is read as printed. It judges nothing, and a tolerance the person gave overrides it

source.citation: the person's standing rule of 2026-11-18 (docs/ideas/20261118.md, 'Tolerances by a standing rule'); JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM), BIPM (read 2026-11-18, https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-jcgm-100-2008-gum)
source.locus: GUM F.2.2.1, The resolution of a digital indication, printed page 64: with a resolution dx the value lies with equal probability between X - dx/2 and X + dx/2; the last printed digit's unit is the resolution, so half of it is the half-width the rule takes

note: Asked of the meta role in meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261118-design-macbook-20261117-1-5.json (76ba4c5). The rule's two ways are the person's; the half-width of the second is the GUM's interval for a resolution. No value of a source stands behind the worked cases but the person's own example of 1066 K: each is worked by hand in its worked field.
